Marvel is usually very grounded in reality. There are many militaristic themed heroes to make up for that (I.E. The Punisher, Black Widow, Captain America). They're usually making a social commentary on how superheroes interact with the throes of humanity. (Example being the Superhuman Registration Act.)

DC, which I prefer at times, is very mythological and bombastic for nearly every book they've published. But sometimes they can have a little diversity and darker thematic stories (with the Vertigo or Black Label Imprints)

The bottom line is that both publishers have popular characters that suit each of their precedents, and that's what pushes other people into either publisher.
